item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Skills in Copilot Chat
item.description:
[What and why:]

We are introducing skills in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Skills let you customize Copilot Chat with task-specific instructions to improve workflow accuracy. A skill includes specific instructions and, optionally, supporting files or scripts needed to complete a task. Copilot automatically uses these instructions when a request is relevant to the skill, although end users can disable this automatic invocation.

Here is a summary of the features in this release:

  • Skills for end users: Users can create and edit skills, upload existing skills, and share skills with others. They can use skills deployed by their admin or public skills published by Independent Software Vendors. Users can choose whether Copilot can automatically invoke skills or explicitly select one from the new “Agents and Skills” section in Context IQ. For more information about the Context IQ experience, see the related Message Center post MC1479519.
  • Skill deployment by admins: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can deploy, install, or block skills and plugins that contain skills and connectors. With this release, these plugins will be available in both Copilot Chat and Copilot Cowork. For more information about centralized plugin controls, see our recent announcement on plugins. Admins can also use the Tools view to review all skills created by users in Copilot Chat.
  • Agent Store to include plugins: The “Agent store” in Copilot Chat is evolving to include plugins; see our recent announcement on plugins for context. With this release, users can discover agents, skills, and plugins containing skills in the Store. Discoverability of connector-only plugins in Store is not part of this release and will be added as a follow up, making all plugins available there. Until then, connectors will remain available through the Data Sources menu in Chat.
  • Use across Cowork and Chat: Skills created in Copilot Chat can also be used in Cowork. Plugins deployed from the Microsoft 365 admin center will be available in both Copilot Chat and Copilot Cowork. However, skills created in Copilot Cowork are available in Copilot Chat only if they are shared.
  • Developer tools: User-built skills and plugins created with WIQ Dev Tools or Agents Toolkit will also be available in Copilot Chat.

Skills in Copilot Chat will roll out to Information Barriers tenants in November. In tenants where Information Barriers are enabled, users can create skills for personal use and use skills deployed by their admin or use public skills published by Independent Software Vendors. Sharing user-created skills is not currently supported but will be enabled in the future in accordance with Information Barriers policies.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Copilot Chat users can create, upload, and edit skills, and use skills and plugins published by ISVs or deployed by admins. Admins can publish, install, block, and review skills and plugins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Support for Information Barriers tenants will roll out in November. Users in these tenants can create skills for personal use and use skills and plugins published by ISVs or deployed by admins, but they cannot share user-created skills at this time.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

To deploy a plugin that contains skills, go to the Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Upload. Upload the plugin app package, publish or install it for the intended users or groups. Review the skills created by users in Copilot Chat by reviewing the skills and plugins inventory in Tools on Microsoft Admin Center

[Compliance considerations:]

This feature follows its parent service's data residency and processing commitments.

This feature supports role-based access control (RBAC).

Customer administrators can control user access to this feature using the following interfaces: Admin UI, Admins have user/group granularity for controlling access to the service.

The newly created objects appear in the following inventories: Microsoft 365 admin center Tools Registry

item.title: [stayInformed] Audio Overview Updates
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is rolling out new capabilities in Audio Overview to make it easier to navigate longer content, support enterprise information protection, and create audio overviews from more types of content.

Episodes

For longer and more content-rich notebooks, Audio Overview can organize the discussion into topic-based episodes. This makes it easier for users to navigate the audio and focus on different parts of the content.

Sensitivity labels when saving to OneDrive

Audio Overviews now support Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels when saved to OneDrive. If the source content includes sensitivity labels, the saved Audio Overview inherits the most restrictive label from its sources. Sensitivity labels apply to the saved file in OneDrive. Audio Overviews within the notebook are not yet sensitivity labeled.

More supported content types

Audio Overview can now understand and ground its discussion in additional types of content added to a notebook, including:

  • OneNote pages
  • Loop pages
  • Plain text (.txt) files
  • Emails
  • Teams meetings
  • Teams chats

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who create and consume Audio Overviews.
  • Organizations that use Audio Overview with Microsoft 365 content stored or saved in OneDrive.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Audio Overview
  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels

What will happen:

  • Users can navigate longer Audio Overviews through topic-based episodes.
  • Users can create Audio Overviews grounded in additional content types, including OneNote pages, Loop pages, .txt files, emails, Teams meetings, and Teams chats.
  • Audio Overviews saved to OneDrive from labeled source content will inherit the most restrictive sensitivity label from the sources.
  • This release does not introduce sensitivity labeling for Audio Overviews while they remain within the notebook.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required to prepare for this update. These Audio Overview improvements will roll out automatically to eligible users.

For sensitivity labels, when an Audio Overview is saved to OneDrive from labeled source content, the saved file will automatically inherit the most restrictive sensitivity label from its sources. No additional configuration is required as part of this feature rollout.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Audio Overview uses AI capabilities to generate audio grounded in Microsoft 365 content, including additional supported content types.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can create and navigate Audio Overviews from more supported Microsoft 365 content sources.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable Purview capabilities such as Information Protection labels?Yes. Audio Overviews saved to OneDrive from labeled source content inherit the most restrictive sensitivity label from the sources.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Graph: New tenant controls for retirement of non-standard file API tokens
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is retiring pre-authenticated URLs, also known as tempauth URLs, from SharePoint Online and OneDrive. Beginning April 1, 2027, selected Microsoft Graph file APIs will no longer return URLs that contain embedded authentication information and will no longer issue HTTP 302 redirects to those URLs.

To help organizations prepare, new SharePoint Online tenant controls are coming soon in a future release of Microsoft SharePoint Online PowerShell. These controls will allow administrators to enable updated Microsoft Graph URL behavior for specific applications before the retirement date. This gives organizations time to validate application compatibility, improve security posture, and transition to standard Microsoft Entra ID authentication before the change takes effect.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Service change (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in early April 2027 and expected to complete in late April 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Administrators responsible for Microsoft Graph, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, application integrations, and tenant security
  • Owners of third-party applications, line-of-business applications, custom applications, and automation solutions that use affected Microsoft Graph file APIs
  • Organizations using applications that follow redirects or rely on URLs containing embedded authentication information

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Graph
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Third-party and custom applications that consume Microsoft Graph file APIs

What will happen

Applications using affected Microsoft Graph APIs may currently receive:

  • SharePoint Online download, upload, monitor, preview, version, or similar URLs that contain temporary authentication information.
  • Media service URLs that contain temporary authentication information.
  • HTTP 302 redirects to URLs containing embedded authentication information.

After the change:

  • Applications configured to use supported Microsoft Graph URL alternatives will receive Microsoft Graph URLs and continue authenticating with Microsoft Graph access tokens.
  • APIs that currently return HTTP 302 redirects to temporary authentication URLs will instead return content directly.
  • SharePoint Online URLs returned by affected APIs will no longer contain embedded temporary authentication information.
  • Applications accessing SharePoint Online URLs directly will need a valid Microsoft Entra ID access token for the SharePoint Online resource.
  • Requests made directly to SharePoint APIs rather than through Microsoft Graph are not affected by the tenant control setting.
  • Applications that store, inspect, or redeem URLs containing embedded authentication tokens may stop functioning if not updated before April 1, 2027.
  • The change is not enabled by default through tenant controls. Administrators must choose which application IDs participate in testing and validation.

Affected API families include:

  • File download and content APIs
  • createUploadSession APIs
  • Copy APIs and long-running action monitors
  • Preview APIs
  • Thumbnail APIs
  • Version APIs
  • Format conversion APIs

[Action required and recommendations]

Administrators should begin validation before April 1, 2027.

Recommended actions:

  • Identify applications that obtain file, version, thumbnail, preview, upload-session, or copy-operation URLs through Microsoft Graph.
  • Review whether applications inspect, store, or redeem URLs containing embedded authentication information.
  • Verify that applications can process direct content responses instead of relying on HTTP 302 redirects.
  • Confirm applications can obtain and send the appropriate Microsoft Entra ID access token when calling Microsoft Graph or SharePoint Online endpoints.
  • Enable the new tenant setting for a limited set of application IDs and validate application behavior.
  • Monitor application errors, authentication failures, and sign-in activity during testing.
  • Expand the configuration to additional applications after successful validation.
  • Contact application vendors and internal application owners to confirm support plans and timelines for affected applications.
  • Communicate this upcoming change to development and application support teams.

No action is required if:

  • Your organization does not use the affected APIs.
  • Applications already use direct Microsoft Graph content endpoints and standard Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

Learn more

  • Clear-SPOTenantPreAuthSettings (Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell) | Microsoft Learn
  • Get-SPOTenantPreAuthSettings (Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell) | Microsoft Learn
  • Get started with the SharePoint Online Management Shell | Microsoft Learn
  • OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect protocols - Microsoft identity platform | Microsoft Learn
  • Pre-authenticated (tempauth) URLs are retiring: move to Microsoft Entra ID tokens before April 1, 2027 - Microsoft 365 Developer Blog

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. New SharePoint Online tenant controls are being introduced to allow administrators to opt specific application IDs into the updated authentication behavior before the retirement date. Customers should review documentation to determine available scoping and configuration options. Regarding controlled by EntraID Group membership, I do not think that applies. These are SharePoint Online PowerShell cmdlets.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Planner: Introducing Local Custom Fields
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing Custom Fields in Microsoft Planner, enabling users to tailor plans to match the way their teams work. Users can add Text, Number, Date, Yes/No, and Choice fields to capture information that matters to their workflows and manage that information across Board, Grid, and Task details.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by early November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Planner Premium P1, P3, or P5 license
  • Users with a Microsoft 365 license

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Planner

What will happen

  • Users with a Planner Premium P1, P3, or P5 license will be able to create, edit, and manage Custom Fields and their values.
  • Users with a Microsoft 365 license can view Custom Fields and values as read-only and export them but cannot create or edit them.
  • Users can add up to 10 custom fields with 255 characters each to tasks in a plan for information beyond Planner's built-in fields. Available types are Text, Number, Date, Yes/No, and Choice, and field names can be up to 255 characters.
  • Choice fields are single-select and can contain 2 to 25 colored options.
  • Field values can be viewed and updated across Board, Grid, and Task details and used for sorting, filtering, grouping, and bulk editing.
  • This feature is optional. Existing plans are not affected unless users add Custom Fields.
  • Existing compliance capabilities cover custom field data, including Unified Audit Log, eDiscovery, Microsoft Information Protection through inherited plan-level labels, and Data Lifecycle Management.

[Action required and recommendations]

No tenant-level configuration or admin setup is required to enable Custom Fields. We recommend that you:

  • Ensure users who need to create or edit Custom Fields have a Planner Premium P1, P3, or P5 license. Microsoft 365 users will have read-only access.
  • Inform users about the supported field types, the limit of 10 fields per plan, and that Choice fields are single-select with 2 to 25 options.
  • Advise users that deleting a custom field or choice option is permanent and cannot be undone, and that deleting a choice option clears affected values.
  • Remind users to follow your organization's data-handling policies. Custom field data is included in audit, eDiscovery, Microsoft Information Protection, and data lifecycle processes.

[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change store new customer data?

  • Yes. Custom field names and values that users create on tasks (up to 10 fields per plan) are stored as part of plan/task data.

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)? 

  • No. Existing task and plan data is unchanged. Custom fields are additive metadata on tasks.

Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable any of the following Microsoft Purview capabilities?

  • Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies or enforcement
    • No.
  • Information Protection labels or sensitive information types
    • No.
  • Conditional Access policies
    • No.
  • Audit logging capabilities
    • No. Custom field edits are logged in Task History and flow to the Unified Audit Log.
  • eDiscovery or Content Search
    • No.
  • Encryption methods or key management
    • No. Data uses existing service encryption.
  • Retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows
    • No. Custom field data follows the existing task/plan lifecycle (deleted when the task/plan is deleted).

Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities (e.g., Purview or admin reporting)?

  • No. Existing Purview and admin reporting continue to work; custom field activity appears in audit logs like other task edits.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. Users can view, edit, and export custom field values (Export to Excel), and the data is deleted along with the task or plan it belongs to.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Outlook: Themes by Copilot retirement
item.description:
[What and why]

We are retiring Themes by Copilot in Microsoft Outlook. Themes by Copilot currently allows users with a Copilot license to create and apply a Copilot-generated theme in Settings. As part of this change, Themes by Copilot will be removed from Settings, and users will no longer be able to select or return to a Theme by Copilot after changing to a different theme.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Retirement begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Copilot license.

Platforms and services

  • New Outlook for Windows
  • Outlook for Android
  • Outlook for iOS
  • Outlook for Mac
  • Outlook on the web

What will happen

  • Themes by Copilot will be removed from Settings. Users who are currently using a Theme by Copilot will retain their current theme until they change it.
  • Themes by Copilot configured to automatically refresh will remain applied but will stop refreshing. Users will retain the current theme imagery until they change their theme.
  • Users can change from their existing Theme by Copilot to a non-Copilot theme but cannot return to a Theme by Copilot after doing so.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Authenticated password change in My Sign-Ins
item.description:
Updated October 9, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why]

We're introducing a new Microsoft Entra capability that Allow password change after secure sign-in directly from My Sign-Ins using an existing strong credential, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business. Users can complete this action even if they don't know their current password and without using self-service password reset (SSPR) or contacting the helpdesk.

Many organizations are adopting allowed password changes after secure sign-ins but still maintain passwords for legacy applications and services. This update helps reduce password-related support requests and removes a common barrier to adoption. The feature is disabled by default and requires administrator enablement before users can access it.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Beginning end of October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators who manage password change settings
  • Users who have a registered allowed password change after secure sign-in method (passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business) and also maintain a password
  • Organizations that choose to enable the feature

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Entra
  • My Sign-Ins (mysignins.microsoft.com)

What will happen

  • Because this feature is off by default, there is no change to your users' experience unless you turn it on. 
  • After the feature is enabled, eligible users will see a new Change password option in My Sign-Ins.
  • Users can authenticate set a new password without knowing their existing password.
  • Users are not required to enroll in or use SSPR to complete this action.
  • Administrators can choose to enable or disable the capability through Microsoft Entra management interfaces available at release.
  • Authentication continues to require a strong password change method, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business.
  • The setting is tenant-wide: you can turn it on for your entire tenant or leave it off for everyone. There is no per-user or per-group scoping. 

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No action is required.

If your organization plans to support allowed password changes after secure sign-in:

  • Review your password management and allowed password changes after secure sign-in strategy.
  • Evaluate whether enabling this capability aligns with your organization's security and support requirements.
  • Communicate the new self-service capability to helpdesk and support teams.
  • Update internal user guidance and documentation as needed.
  • If your organization chooses to offer allowed password changes after secure sign-in, enable the feature through the Microsoft Entra admin experience or supported APIs when it becomes available in October 2026.

Learn more 

  • Microsoft Learn documentation will be available when the feature releases in October. 

[Compliance Considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. The feature is disabled by default and requires explicit administrator enablement.
Does the change modify how users can access or correct their personal data?Yes. Users gain a new self-service method to update their password using an existing allowed password change after secure sign-in.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Removing Copilot from the chat list
item.description:
Updated October 8, 2026: After additional consideration we have decided not to proceed with this change. You can safely disregard this message. We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.

[What and why]

To provide a more consistent and streamlined Microsoft 365 Copilot experience in Microsoft Teams, we are simplifying how users access Copilot in Teams.

Today, users can access Copilot either from the Teams chat list or from the Copilot app in the Teams app bar. Beginning in October 2026, we will remove the Copilot entry point from the Teams chat list and direct users to access Copilot through the Copilot app. The Copilot app provides access to the full set of Copilot capabilities, while the chat list entry point provides a more limited experience.

This change creates a single, consistent access point for Copilot in Teams, helping users discover and return to Copilot more easily while reducing interface clutter. To help users transition, a coachmark will direct users from the chat list entry point to the Copilot app before the chat list entry point is removed.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Copilot chat list entry point removal (Worldwide, GCC): Cancelled

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations whose users access Microsoft 365 Copilot in Microsoft Teams
  • Users of Microsoft Teams desktop and web applications who currently access Copilot from the Teams chat list.
  • Mobile users are not affected.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams desktop
  • Microsoft Teams web

What will happen

  • The Copilot entry point in the Teams chat list will be removed. 
  • Prior to the mid-October removal, users who access Copilot from the chat list will see a coachmark directing them to the Copilot app.
  • The Copilot app in the Teams app bar will remain available and unchanged.
  • If the Copilot app has been unpinned from the Teams app bar, users will be directed to the app overflow menu where they can locate the Copilot app.
  • Existing Copilot conversations, notifications, supported deep links, and session continuity will continue to work.
  • No user conversations, prompts, chat history, or Copilot data will be removed.
  • Mobile experiences are unchanged.
  • This change is enabled by Microsoft and does not require tenant configuration.

Before:

 

After:

 

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Inform users that Copilot in Teams will be accessed through the Copilot app in the Teams app bar going forward.
  • Update internal training materials, screenshots, adoption content, and support documentation that reference the Copilot chat list entry point.
  • Notify help desk and support teams before rollout.
  • Review Teams app setup policies and consider pinning the Copilot app for users if it is not already pinned.
  • Monitor user feedback after rollout and direct users to the Copilot app if they are looking for the retired chat list entry point.

Learn more

  • Pin Microsoft Copilot Chat in the Microsoft 365 apps | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft PowerPoint for Windows: Improved slide contextual menu consistency
item.description:
[What and why]

We are updating the contextual menu for slides in Microsoft PowerPoint for Windows to make it more complete and consistent. Common slide actions will be available directly where users are working and organized in a more predictable order, helping users find frequent tasks faster.

As part of this update, due to low usage, the Photo Album... command will be removed from the contextual menu but will remain accessible through the Insert tab in the ribbon. This update will be enabled by default for all users and ships via standard staged rollout. There are no new SKU, licensing, tenant, geography, or admin controls, and files, data, security, and compliance are not affected by this update.

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

Platforms and services

What will happen

  • The slide contextual menu and slide thumbnail contextual menu will be updated to be more complete and reorganized in a more predictable order for greater consistency.
  • The Photo Album… command will be removed from the contextual menus due to low usage but will remain available on the Insert tab in the ribbon. All other commands will remain available, although some commands may appear in a different position within the contextual menus.
  • This update is enabled by default for all users and ships via standard staged rollout without introducing new SKUs, licensing, tenant, geography, or admin controls, or changes to files, data, security, or compliance.

[Action required and recommendations]

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft API Hub: Zendesk OAuth tokens will require expiration and automatic refresh
item.description:

item.description:

When users paste slides using Keep Source Formatting, PowerPoint will now import only the slide masters and layouts required for the pasted slides instead of importing all slide masters and layouts from the source presentation.

This change helps reduce presentation file size, improve performance when opening large presentations, and enhance collaboration experiences such as co-authoring by minimizing unnecessary design content in presentations. Users who prefer the previous behavior can continue using it through a setting that allows them to choose their preferred slide paste experience.

  • When users paste slides with Keep Source Formatting, PowerPoint will import only the slide masters and layouts required by the pasted slides.
  • Presentation file sizes may be reduced because unnecessary slide masters and layouts will no longer be imported by default.
  • By minimizing unnecessary design content, smaller presentations may open faster and perform better during collaboration and co-authoring scenarios.
  • Users who prefer the previous behavior can continue using it through a setting that allows them to bring over all slide masters and layouts from the source presentation.

As communicated in MC1454108, beginning in early September, 2026, Microsoft will start redirecting users from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft in organizations where access to copilot.cloud.microsoft is available. Organizations who may have blocked connection to copilot.cloud.microsoft will be redirected in October.

Backend services and Copilot in Edge will require connection to *.cloud.microsoft. To avoid disruption to Copilot access across the web app, desktop app, and Edge experience, review your organization's network and security controls to confirm that users can connect to *.cloud.microsoft.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • In early September, 2026, Microsoft will redirect users from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft in organizations where access to copilot.cloud.microsoft is available.  
  • In early November, 2026 Microsoft will redirect the remaining users who had not been redirected in early September. If your organization cannot complete the required configuration before the redirect, contact your Microsoft account representative to discuss available options. 

[Impact on your organization:]

When the Copilot web app transitions from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft, users will be automatically redirected. If device, network, proxy, firewall, security gateway, or similar controls block URLs within *.cloud.microsoft, affected users may be unable to use Copilot in the web app, desktop app, and Microsoft Edge experience. Review these controls and allow the required domain before the redirect begins.

The redirect remains within the *.cloud.microsoft domain and retains its security, compliance, and enterprise allow-listing properties. Organizations that follow the recommendednetwork configurations for Microsoft 365 Copilot do not need additional network changes. 

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • You can validate connectivity to the *.cloud.microsoft domain by using the Microsoft 365 Connectivity Test tool. Use the connectivity tool to validate connectivity to *.cloud.microsoft and confirm that your network and security controls allow access before the redirect applies to your organization. If you find out your organization blocks connection to *.cloud.microsoft, contact your Microsoft account representative before September 10, 2026 to discuss available options.
  • Confirm that copilot.cloud.microsoft is not blocked in your environment. Review legacy filtering rules, URL category restrictions, proxy policies, firewall rules, tenant restrictions, Conditional Access policies, and app control policies, and update them if needed. 
  • Add *.cloud.microsoft to your organization’s allow lists. If you have questions about tenant-specific network configurations and allow list requirements, you can contact your Microsoft support team for guidance based on your specific environment. Note: Microsoft does not support allowing partial or only selected Microsoft 365 application URLs within the *.cloud.microsoft domain. Allow the entire *.cloud.microsoft domain to maintain service reliability and avoid disruptions. 
  • Confirm that your environment aligns with the recommended network requirements for Microsoft 365 Copilot. 
  • Coordinate with teams that manage network security, proxy services, firewalls, secure web gateways, SSE/SASE platforms, or third-party filtering solutions to ensure traffic to *.cloud.microsoft is permitted. 
  • If preventing personal Microsoft account sign-ins is the reason your organization blocks copilot.cloud.microsoft, consider using TenantRestrictions as the targeted control. This control allows your organization to restrict authentication with personal Microsoft accounts on managed networks or devices, while still permitting access to the Copilot service URL.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Entra ID: Passkey support for B2B users
item.description:
Updated October 8, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra ID will support passkey registration and sign-in for B2B users, including internal guest users and external users. Eligible B2B users will be able to register and use passkeys issued by the resource tenant to satisfy that tenant's multifactor authentication (MFA) requirements.

Passkeys are already supported for member users in their home tenant. Until now, B2B users could not use a resource tenant passkey when that tenant required MFA and did not trust the home tenant's MFA. This update closes that gap and gives guest and external users a phishing-resistant way to satisfy MFA requirements in the resource tenant.

B2B users can register a resource tenant passkey from the resource tenant's My Security Info page, during a proof-up prompt, or through a passkey registration campaign. Once registered, the passkey can satisfy the resource tenant's MFA requirements during sign-in.

Microsoft Authenticator app passkeys will be supported for internal guest users but not for external users.

Important: This rollout intersects with the previously announced retirement of SMS and voice authentication. As described in Message Center posts MC1426371 and MC1434201, any user enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies will be automatically enabled for all passkey types. This will include eligible B2B users when B2B passkey support becomes available.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (GCC, Worldwide): Beginning in late October 2026, with a phased rollout as outlined below:

  • Internal guest users: Beginning in late October 2026 (previously early October) and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously late October)
  • External users (excluding Microsoft Authenticator app passkeys): Rollout timing will be communicated in a future Message center post update.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators managing Authentication methods policies
  • Organizations that use Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration
  • Internal guest users and external users who are in scope for passkey authentication
  • Internal guest users and external users who are enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • My Security Info
  • Authentication methods policy
  • Conditional Access

What will happen

  • The feature will be enabled by default.
  • B2B users who are already in scope for passkeys in your Authentication methods policy will automatically be able to register and sign in with resource tenant passkeys.
  • Eligible B2B users may receive prompts to register a passkey during sign-in through proof-up experiences or passkey registration campaigns, if those experiences are configured in your tenant.
  • Users can also register a passkey from the resource tenant's My Security Info page.
  • If your organization has excluded B2B users from passkeys in the Authentication methods policy, and those users are not separately subject to automatic passkey enablement through the SMS and voice retirement changes, they will not be prompted and will not be able to register or sign in with a resource tenant passkey.
  • Under the SMS and voice retirement changes described in MC1426371 and MC1434201, B2B users who are enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies will be automatically enabled for all passkey types. Excluding these users from the passkey policy alone will not prevent this automatic enablement if they remain enabled for SMS or voice.
  • This change gives guest and external users a phishing-resistant sign-in option and helps organizations extend strong authentication requirements to their B2B population.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that administrators review current passkey and MFA configurations before rollout:

  • Review your Authentication methods policy. Confirm which users are in scope for passkeys, including guest and external users. B2B users who are in scope will be enabled automatically. Exclude them from the policy if that is not the intended behavior.
  • Review Message Center posts MC1426371 and MC1434201 for details about the SMS and voice retirement changes.
  • Review SMS and voice assignments in both the Authentication methods policy and legacy MFA policies. If you do not want specific B2B users to be automatically enabled for all passkey types, move those users off SMS and voice in all applicable policies. Excluding them only from the passkey policy is not sufficient while they remain enabled for SMS or voice.
  • Review your passkey registration campaign. Confirm that the campaign's user scope includes the intended users.
  • Review your Conditional Access policies. Confirm that MFA and authentication strength requirements will apply as intended for B2B users when resource tenant passkeys become available.
  • Confirm user scoping across authentication-related policies. Make sure the groups and user types targeted by each policy align with your organization's requirements for guest and external users.

Consider notifying your help desk and identity support teams that eligible B2B users may begin receiving passkey registration prompts after rollout.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Passkey credential registration data may be stored as part of Microsoft Entra authentication management.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?The change introduces an additional authentication method for B2B users accessing resource tenant resources.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method
item.description:
Updated October 8, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Users will soon be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor authentication method. Previously, people had to set up an alternate MFA method like SMS or Voice before they could add a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO. That extra step pushed users toward weaker methods and slowed the move to phishing-resistant sign-in. Now password-only users can go straight to a passkey, making it easier to adopt strong authentication from day one. As part of this work, we will also be enabling Authenticator App passwordless sign-in to be a user's first registered MFA method. 

[Rollout schedule]

This feature will roll out in phases: 

Phase 1: Support for synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows, and FIDO2 security keys.  

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 (previously early October) and expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November). 

Phase 2: Support for Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, Authenticator App passkey, and Authenticator App passwordless sign-in. 

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early January 2026 and expect to complete by late February 2027. 

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who have not yet registered a multifactor authentication method
  • Identity and security administrators responsible for authentication onboarding and registration policies

  • Users will no longer need to register a method such as SMS or voice before registering a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, or Authenticator passwordless sign-in.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: Retiring legacy sign-in implementation on Windows
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Edge is retiring its legacy direct-WAM sign-in implementation on Windows starting with Microsoft Edge version 157, completing the consolidation onto the OneAuth authentication library.

This change standardizes authentication flows across Microsoft 365 client applications, simplifies platform supportability, eliminates dual-stack authentication code paths, and provides improved diagnostic and recovery mechanisms. Windows Web Account Manager (WAM) itself is not being deprecated; OneAuth continues to use Windows WAM.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete in early November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using Microsoft Edge on Windows.
  • Users with Edge profiles that have not yet automatically migrated to OneAuth.
  • Organizations that explicitly disabled OneAuth WAM using --disable-features=msOneAuthWAM.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Edge on Windows
  • Browser sign-in, identity, token fetch, Single Sign-On, and account synchronization experiences

What will happen:

  • Starting with Microsoft Edge version 157, all remaining profiles will transition directly to OneAuth authentication.
  • The fallback legacy WAM path will default off under all circumstances.
  • Most users will transition transparently.
  • In rare cases, users may need to sign in to Microsoft Edge again.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

We recommend that admins identify unmigrated profiles and test the transition before Microsoft Edge version 157 reaches their environment.

  • Navigate to edge://signin-internals in Microsoft Edge.
  • Under Edge Auth Library Information > Library, confirm whether the profile shows OneAuth or WAM.
  • If OneAuth is displayed, the profile is already using the modern path and no action is required.
  • If WAM is displayed, the profile is still using the legacy path.

On pilot test devices running Microsoft Edge version 155 or later, admins can test the transition before version 157 by launching Edge with this force flag:

msedge.exe --enable-features=msForceOneAuthWAM

Verify that edge://signin-internals reflects OneAuth, and confirm that browser sign-in, Single Sign-On, and account synchronization work as expected.

Inform support teams that a small number of users might see a sign-in action on the profile menu after updating to Edge version 157. If users experience sign-in issues, collect OneAuth logs with:

msedge.exe --enable-features=msForceOneAuthWAM --enable-logging -v=1 --oneauth-log-level=5

Default log location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\chrome_debug.log

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Admins can validate and manage the transition through Microsoft Edge configuration and feature flags. Review your Microsoft Edge deployment and policy management practices for group-based rollout controls.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft 365: The Next Generation of File & Folder Sharing
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default. At the center of this update is a new hero link—a single sharing link that controls access to a file or folder.

Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL. The hero link consolidates sharing controls into a single link that can be updated after it has been shared, reducing the need to create and resend new links when access requirements change.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rolling out early October 2026 (previously mid-September) through end of November 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365.

Platforms and services: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 file-sharing experiences.

What will happen:

  • Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.
  • The hero link settings determine who can access the item beyond people who are explicitly granted access.
  • Adding people directly to a file or folder remains unchanged and continues to be the simplest way to share content.

Screenshot - Add people screen when sharing 

  • By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

Screenshot - Share file view with hero link

  • Users can broaden access to people in the organization with the link or, where permitted by organizational policy, to anyone with the link.
  • Users can choose whether recipients can view, edit, or view without downloading, depending on available permissions.
  • Changing the audience for the hero link updates the existing link rather than creating a new one.
  • If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.
  • Existing sharing links will continue to function and will appear under Other links in the sharing dialog.
  • Effective access remains the most permissive combination of direct permissions, inherited permissions, group-based permissions, and link-based permissions.
  • Users will see a tutorial experience upon opening the new share dialog for the first time.

[Action required/Recommendations:]

No action is required before rollout.

Organizations should consider the following preparation activities:

  • Review internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation to reflect the new single-link sharing model.
  • Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.
  • Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.

Learn more:

  • Walkthrough Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3RpE0KrQmcA&t=4s
  • Announcement Blog: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/onedriveblog/simple-smart-and-secure-the-next-step-in-sharing-files-in-microsoft-365/4411655

Admin controls

  • Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.
  • Supported values are:
    • OnlyPeopleAdded (default)
    • Organization
  • There is currently no tenant-wide equivalent setting for the hero link audience.
  • DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.
  • Hero links start with view permissions by default.
  • Existing default sharing link settings and link expiration policies continue to apply to legacy links and do not govern hero links.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

We are expanding report publishing capabilities in Microsoft Viva Insights to include leaders, such as chief officers, managers, and their delegates. As part of this update, in Viva Feature Access Management, the Analyst report publish setting will be renamed to Report publish. This setting, which is on by default, will continue to be managed by Global Admins and Insights Admins, and will govern publishing for both analysts and leaders. This update enables leaders to directly publish and distribute curated Power BI reports available in Viva Insights without requiring an analyst to publish on their behalf.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Viva Insights report publishing capabilities.
  • Analysts, chief officers, managers, delegates, Insights Admins, and Global Admins.
  • Users who receive published Viva Insights reports.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Viva Insights
  • Power BI reports available through the Viva Insights Reports tab

What will happen

  • All analysts and leaders will be able to publish Power BI reports that are available to them in the Reports tab.
  • Users can publish either default or customized reports available to them.
  • Publishers can define the audience, report title, description, and publication end date.
  • Recipients will receive an email notification when a report is published to them, and can access published reports from the Viva Insights Reports tab.
  • Published reports can be shared using either: 
    • Unfiltered publish, where recipients view the report using the full data scope available for that report.
    • Manager-hierarchy publish, where recipients view the report based on the applicable manager hierarchy.
  • If a published report is configured to refresh weekly or monthly, the underlying query will continue to refresh until the publication end date.
  • Analysts and leaders will be able to manage published reports through the Manage publishes option.
  • Recipients can view and interact with published reports but cannot download reports, access row-level data, modify or manage publications, extend access, or republish reports.
  • If a publisher loses the qualifying role used to publish the report, recipients will retain access until the publication expires.
  • The existing Analyst report publish feature access control will be renamed to Report publish. This control will govern report publishing for analysts and leader personas, remains managed by Global Admins and Insights Admins, and is on by default.
  • Insights Admins will have visibility into published reports through the Admin Publish Reports experience, including the ability to view and remove publications and publish reports on behalf of users.

Setting up report properties prior to publishing

View and manage published reports

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you review your organization's report publishing governance and processes prior to rollout.

[Learn more]

  • Publish reports | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Backup: Activity Logs
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing activity logs in Microsoft 365 Backup to help administrators monitor backup policy and restore activities directly within the product. Activity logs provide greater visibility into configuration changes, restore progress, failures, and operational status without requiring administrators to leave the Microsoft 365 Backup experience.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Administrators who manage Microsoft 365 Backup

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Backup
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Exchange Online

What will happen

  • Activity logs will be available for Microsoft 365 Backup actions across supported workloads, including SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Exchange Online.
  • Activity log entries will include metadata such as service, activity type, status, impact, policy or restore task details, timestamps, and the administrator who performed the action.
  • Administrators will be able to:
    • Filter logs by service, activity type, activity status, impact, and date range.
    • Search activity logs using free text.
    • Export filtered or searched logs to CSV for offline review, reporting, and compliance workflows.
  • Role-based access controls will apply. Administrators will only be able to view logs for workloads they are authorized to manage.
  • To access this feature:

1. Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center.

2. Open Microsoft 365 Backup.

3. Select Recent activities to open the Activity logs page.

4. Use the date selector, search, or filters to review activity. Select Export to download the current result.

Activity logs in the Microsoft 365 admin center

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you inform your backup administrators that activity monitoring for Microsoft 365 Backup will be available directly within the product.

We will update this post with new documentation.

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft OneDrive: New pay-as-you-go storage billing option
item.description:

We will communicate via a separate Message center post at a later date once we are ready to proceed with gov cloud release. If you are in a gov cloud, you can safely disregard this message. [What and why]

We are introducing a pay-as-you-go, consumption-based billing option for additional OneDrive storage. This capability gives administrators more flexibility to manage storage growth by allowing selected OneDrive accounts to exceed their licensed storage quotas when needed, while helping organizations control which users can consume additional storage beyond their licensed storage quotas. [Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): The public preview of this feature is available now to all commercial tenants.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 commercial tenant administrators who manage OneDrive storage.
  • Organizations with OneDrive users approaching or exceeding their licensed storage quotas.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft 365 admin and storage management experiences

What will happen

  • Administrators will be able to control which accounts are enabled to use a pay-as-you-go model to provide additional OneDrive storage beyond their licensed storage quotas.
  • Accounts enabled for storage consumption above their licensed storage quotas will be billed automatically based on usage.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if you do not wish to use pay-as-you-go storage for your organization. We recommend that you:

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Connected Platforms - Agent 365 extends observability to third-party agents
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline and content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft will roll out third-party agent observability in Microsoft Agent 365 to tenants. This lets you monitor the agents you sync from Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Anthropic Claude through Connected platforms in the same place as your Microsoft agents.

Administrators can see runs, sessions, tool calls, and exceptions on each agent’s Activity tab. The result: a more consistent way to understand agent usage and investigate issues across supported platforms without treating every environment as a separate monitoring exercise.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on late October 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by late October 2026 (previously late September).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out late November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected

  • Administrators using Microsoft Agent 365 and Connected platforms
  • Organizations synchronizing agents from Amazon Bedrock Classic, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Google Vertex AI, or Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Agent 365
  • Connected platforms
  • Amazon Bedrock Classic
  • Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
  • Google Vertex AI
  • Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview)

What will happen

  • Agent 365 can collect observability data from supported third-party agent platforms.
  • Collected activity appears on each synchronized agent's Activity tab.
  • Runs, sessions, tool calls, and exceptions are mapped to the Agent 365 observability model.
  • Existing connections continue syncing agents as they do today.
  • Collection remains disabled for existing connections until an administrator enables it.
  • A new Collect agent observability data setting is available when creating or editing a supported connection.
  • The setting is enabled by default for new connections.
  • Agent 365 reads activity using existing connection credentials and does not execute agents.
  • Third-party providers may charge for tracing, storage, logging, or query services.
  • The Users metric is unavailable for synchronized third-party agents because Microsoft Entra identities are not provided by supported platforms.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • No action is required for existing connections.
  • Enable Collect agent observability data on existing connections if observability is desired.
  • Validate source platform permissions and telemetry configuration.
  • Clear the Collect agent observability data option during setup if collection is not desired for a new connection.

Platform Requirements

  • Amazon Bedrock Classic: Enable trace capture to Amazon S3 and grant read access to the activity bucket.
  • Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search and grant access to query CloudWatch log groups.
  • Google Vertex AI: Assign required BigQuery, Monitoring, and Cloud Trace roles; enable APIs; enable telemetry collection and Trace Analytics BigQuery export.
  • Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (preview): No additional setup required.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The feature uses AI/ML or agent capabilities with Microsoft 365 content, prompts, or service data as described in this message.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify any capability that enables users to automate workflows through AI or bot agents?Yes. The feature introduces or updates agent-related AI capabilities as described in this message.
Does the change include an admin control and, can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. The feature includes or affects admin controls, policies, permissions, roles, authentication, or management settings as described in this message. Review the linked documentation or admin center controls for group-based configuration support.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. This change only impacts tenants who have not adjusted the policy that controls file attachment in an external Teams chat. To opt out of this change, disable the capability using the Teams PowerShell setting provided in the “Action required and recommendations” section below. This can be done before the rollout and your policy setting will be respected. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions. 

Prior to this change, when existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies allow, users can already share files in external chats by sharing a link to the file. This update makes that flow easier by adding the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences directly in Teams. Files uploaded from the user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while cloud files remain stored in their existing location. Teams then assigns permissions to chat participants, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing policies. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control.

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • This change applies only to organizations where the setting has not been explicitly configured. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted. 
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants, unless your organization has previously explicitly disabled this setting in Teams. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach and share files using the paperclip option or drag and drop in external (federated) chats.
  • Files shared through these experiences continue to be stored and shared through OneDrive or SharePoint. Files uploaded from a user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while existing cloud files remain in their current location. 
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using paperclip or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files shared through the paperclip or drag-and-drop experience.
  • The files will be shared as hyperlinks after send. 
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

To opt out of this change, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting if you have not already explicitly configured this setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns chat participants access to files shared via paperclip icon, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) [Outlook Mac] Purview Data Loss Prevention support for Calendar Events
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention \(DLP\) policies for calendar events. Organizations can detect and help prevent the sharing of sensitive information in meeting subjects, descriptions, and invite content through policy tips, user remediation, and policy enforcement. This provides consistent compliance protection across email and calendar experiences on Mac devices.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out mid-November 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on your organization:]

This feature helps organizations extend Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention protections to calendar events created in Outlook for Mac. Users receive policy guidance before sending meeting invitations that contain sensitive information, helping reduce accidental data exposure and improve compliance. Organizations benefit from more consistent protection across email and calendar workflows while supporting regulatory and corporate data protection requirements.

[Action required, Recommendations:]

No administrator action is required to prepare for this feature. Existing Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies will automatically apply to supported calendar events in Outlook for Mac. Organizations with DLP policies already configured can benefit from expanded protection of calendar content without additional policy creation or client configuration. Administrators may choose to review existing DLP policies to ensure they align with their organization's compliance requirements.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) [Outlook Mac] Purview DLP Wait-on-Send Support
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention \(DLP\) wait\-on\-send policies. Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete. This helps ensure sensitive information is inspected against organizational policies before messages leave the organization while providing administrators with flexible control over the user experience.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out mid-November 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on your organization:]

This feature helps organizations reduce the risk of sensitive information being sent before Microsoft Purview DLP policies can be evaluated. Administrators can require users to wait for policy inspection and configure the maximum wait time based on organizational requirements. This improves policy enforcement and compliance while allowing organizations to balance security, performance, and user productivity.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Administrators can review their existing Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies and determine whether wait-on-send enforcement is appropriate for their organization. To take advantage of this feature, administrators may enable and configure the desired wait period within supported DLP policies. No changes are required for organizations that do not plan to use wait-on-send enforcement.
